title: Linear checks certify a mod-two inner product
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $2m$, and let $p$ be a Boolean string of length $2m+1$. Suppose the following checks hold for every seed: the seed selecting the first prefix position requires its bit in $p$ to be false; the seed selecting the final prefix position requires its bit to be true; for each $i<m$, one seed requires the product bit of $p$ at position $i$ to equal the AND of the two corresponding bits of $w$; and another requires the two successive prefix bits of $p$, interpreted in $\mathbb F_2$, to differ by the product bit at position $i$. Then the inner product modulo two of the two length-$m$ blocks of $w$, interpreted as a field element, is $1$.
